articles.title: Tata Motors raises Iveco takeover offer price to 14.40 euro per share
No higher bid: Tata Motors’ final price faces crucial test as Iveco shareholders hold the key
Stellantis and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles broaden partnership to develop vehicles in Pune
Tata Motors, Stellantis expand partnership: New deal details explained
Tata Motors sweetens Iveco offer as key investors hold out

article_briefs.brief: Tata Motors’ €3.91‑billion, "best and final" offer of €14.40 a share for Iveco Group has entered a decisive phase, with a key shareholder vote that could lower the minimum acceptance threshold from 95% to 80%. Exor, Iveco’s largest shareholder, holds a 27.06% stake (43% of voting rights) and supports the deal. Around 20% of shares are held by Davidson Kempner, Syquant Capital and Petrus Advisers, whose participation is critical. Analysts note that a failed transaction would hit Iveco harder than Tata Motors.

Stellantis India, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles (TMPV) and its subsidiary Tata Passenger Electric Mobility signed a definitive agreement expanding their long‑standing partnership into advanced vehicle technology and product collaboration. TMPV will give Stellantis access to its product technology and vehicle architecture; vehicles will be manufactured in India at Fiat India Automobiles Private Limited (FIAPL), the 50:50 joint venture between TMPV and Stellantis, targeting more than 50 global markets.

Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Stellantis have formalised an expanded partnership that combines Tata’s vehicle architecture with Stellantis’ global product development expertise. Building on a February 2026 MoU, the definitive agreement focuses on developing vehicles in India for over 50 markets, with manufacturing at the FIAPL 50:50 joint venture, aiming to boost India’s export capacity in the automotive sector.

Tata Motors raised its offer for Iveco to €14.40 per share (a 2% increase) on 9 October, calling it its "best and final" price. Three large shareholders – Davidson Kempner, Syquant Capital and Petrus Advisers – holding about 20.4% of Iveco’s common shares have not tendered, leaving overall acceptance at only 28.4% of shares. Exor has tendered its 27.06% stake. The deal, announced on 30 July 2025 at €3.8 billion (excluding defence), aims to create a global commercial‑vehicle business with roughly €21 billion revenue.

key_points.text: The €14.40 per share offer is final and the deal now depends on shareholder approvals, with a possible reduction of the acceptance threshold from 95% to 80%; Exor holds 27.06% of Iveco shares (43% voting rights) and backs the transaction.
If completed, the acquisition would create a global commercial‑vehicle group with roughly €21 billion in annual revenue and about 5,90,000 vehicles sold each year.
Tata Motors seeks the deal to gain a foothold in Europe and Latin America, broaden its truck and bus portfolio, and support its electric‑vehicle expansion.

Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Stellantis have expanded their partnership to co‑develop vehicles using Tata’s architecture and Stellantis’ engineering, with manufacturing in India at the 50:50 FIAPL joint venture for more than 50 global markets.

industry_context.text: Europe’s commercial‑vehicle market is undergoing a costly transition to cleaner vehicles, making a larger, integrated group strategically valuable for meeting emission targets.

The Tata‑Stellantis collaboration reflects a broader industry trend of global automotive partnerships that share technology platforms and leverage India’s manufacturing capacity for export to multiple markets.

removed.text: Tata Motors increased its offer for Iveco to €14.40 per share, valuing the transaction at €3.91 billion, a 33.47% premium over 17 July 2025 and a 6.77% premium over 29 July 2025; the increase is funded partly by an €85 million credit facility.

Approximately 20% of Iveco’s shares are held by Davidson Kempner, Syquant Capital and Petrus Advisers, whose lack of tendering puts the acquisition at risk; overall acceptance is only 28.4% of shares.

Tata Motors increased its all‑cash voluntary tender offer for Iveco to €14.40 per share, valuing the transaction at €3.91 billion (up from €3.82 billion). The revised price represents a 33.47% premium over Iveco's share price on 17 July 2025 and a 6.77% premium over the price on 29 July 2025. The acceptance period runs from 7 September to 26 October 2026, with an extraordinary general meeting on 16 October. Funding includes an €85 million credit facility with MUFG Bank. Tata Motors said the price will not be increased further.
